commits.message:
[Interpreter] Fix NaN/Inf handling in interpreter float conversions (#12489)

# What does this PR do?

This PR fixes NaN/Inf handling in the interpreter's float conversion
(`_convert_float` in `python/triton/runtime/interpreter.py`). It
consolidates the NaN/Inf conversion fixes from #12488 into this PR, as
requested there; the FP8 overflow-saturation block from #12488 is not
included, since the compiled backends disagree on that behavior (NVIDIA
lowers to `cvt` with `.satfinite`, AMD sets the FP8 clamping mode), so
the interpreter should not pick one.

Two defects are fixed:

1. **FP8 Inf/NaN encodings decoded as finite numbers.** When the source
of a cast was an FP8 value, the interpreter skipped nonfinite handling
entirely, so the FP8 special codes widened into ordinary numbers:
float8e5 `0x7C` (Inf) decoded to 65536, and the FNUZ NaN (the sign bit
alone) decoded as an infinity because its encoding carries no mantissa
bits. Source Inf/NaN detection is now FP8-aware for every format
(float8e5 uses the reserved exponent, float8e4nv has a single NaN code,
the FNUZ formats float8e4b8/float8e5b16 use the sign bit alone,
float8e4b15 has neither), the nonfinite handling runs for FP8 sources,
and the FNUZ NaN gets an explicit significand when it widens.

2. **RTZ downcasts turned small-payload NaNs into infinities.** The
nonfinite block wrote the canonical quiet-NaN significand only in the
RTNE branch. In the RTZ branch (and on the default no-rounding path), a
NaN whose payload falls entirely in the discarded bits kept a zero
significand while its exponent was forced to all ones, which encodes an
infinity: fp32 NaN `0x7F800001` became fp16 `0x7C00` (+Inf) under
`fp_downcast_rounding="rtz"`. NaN inputs whose computed significand is
zero now get the quiet bit in that branch too, the same canonical value
the RTNE branch writes. Payloads that survive the downcast are
preserved, as before.

## Test plan

The interpreter cast path is pure Python, so all of this runs on CPU
with main's `python/` over the 3.8.0 wheel, `TRITON_INTERPRET=1
--device=cpu`:

- New tests: `test_typeconvert_upcast_fp8_special_codes` (moved from
#12488) and `test_typeconvert_downcast_small_payload_nan` — **15
passed** with this PR. Against unpatched main the same selection gives
**9 failed / 6 passed** (the 5 RTZ cases, and 4 of the 5 decode cases;
the float8e4b15 code is finite on main too, since that format has no
special codes).
- Existing groups: the upcast tests pass.
`test_typeconvert_downcast_clamping` shows the same 21 interpreter
failures as unpatched main; those are the FP8 saturation cases,
intentionally out of scope here per the discussion on #12488.
- Differentials against an exact rational reference, from the two
original changes: every FP8 code decoded to float32, 0 mismatches;
fp16→bf16 under RTZ, exactly 14 mismatches on main (payloads 1–7, both
signs), 0 with this PR.

---------

Co-authored-by: Saloni Garg <26901250+saloni-garg@users.noreply.github.com>

     np.testing.assert_array_equal(result, expected)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("src_dtype, codes, expected", [
+    (tl.float8e4nv, [0x7F, 0xFF, 0x7E], [float('nan'), float('nan'), 448.0]),
+    (tl.float8e5, [0x7C, 0xFC, 0x7D], [float('inf'), float('-inf'), float('nan')]),
+    (tl.float8e4b8, [0x80, 0x7F], [float('nan'), 240.0]),
+    (tl.float8e5b16, [0x80, 0x7F], [float('nan'), 57344.0]),
+    (tl.float8e4b15, [0x7F], [1.875]),
+])
+def test_fp8_upcast_special_codes(src_dtype, codes, expected):
+    # The FP8 Inf/NaN encodings must decode as such, not as finite numbers.
+    data = np.array(codes, dtype=np.uint8)
+    result = interpreter._convert_float(data, src_dtype, tl.float32, ir.ROUNDING_MODE.RTNE)
+    for got, want in zip(result.view(np.float32).tolist(), expected):
+        assert (np.isnan(got) and np.isnan(want)) or got == want
+
+

         exponent[zero_significand_index & subnormal_index] = bias_input - bias_output
         significand[subnormal_index] = (significand[subnormal_index] << bit_pos[subnormal_index]) & (
             (1 << input_dtype.fp_mantissa_width) - 1)
+    if input_dtype == tl.float8e4nv:
+        magnitude = input_bin & ((1 << (input_dtype.primitive_bitwidth - 1)) - 1)
+        input_nan = magnitude == (1 << (input_dtype.primitive_bitwidth - 1)) - 1
+        input_inf = np.zeros(input_bin.shape, dtype=bool)
+    elif input_dtype in (tl.float8e4b8, tl.float8e5b16):
+        input_nan = input_bin == (1 << (input_dtype.primitive_bitwidth - 1))
+        input_inf = np.zeros(input_bin.shape, dtype=bool)
+    elif input_dtype == tl.float8e4b15:
+        input_nan = np.zeros(input_bin.shape, dtype=bool)
+        input_inf = np.zeros(input_bin.shape, dtype=bool)
+    else:
+        nonfinite_input = input_exponent == (1 << input_exponent_width) - 1
+        input_nan = nonfinite_input & ((input_bin & ((1 << input_dtype.fp_mantissa_width) - 1)) != 0)
+        input_inf = nonfinite_input & ((input_bin & ((1 << input_dtype.fp_mantissa_width) - 1)) == 0)
     sign_output = sign
     # Include the leading bit and align subnormal results before rounding.
     full_significand = significand | (1 << input_dtype.fp_mantissa_width)
@@ -237,20 +251,20 @@ def _convert_float(input, input_dtype, output_dtype, rounding_mode):
     exponent_output = np.minimum(output_exponent, max_exponent)
     exponent_output[retained < (1 << output_dtype.fp_mantissa_width)] = 0
     significand_output = retained & ((1 << output_dtype.fp_mantissa_width) - 1)
-    if not input_dtype.is_fp8() and not output_dtype.is_fp8():
-        # Reserved source exponents represent infinities/NaNs, not finite exponents.
-        nonfinite = input_exponent == (1 << input_exponent_width) - 1
-        input_nan = nonfinite & ((input_bin & ((1 << input_dtype.fp_mantissa_width) - 1)) != 0)
+    if not output_dtype.is_fp8():
+        nonfinite = input_nan | input_inf
         overflow = (output_exponent >= max_exponent) & ~nonfinite
         if rounding_mode == _ir.ROUNDING_MODE.RTNE:
             exponent_output[overflow] = max_exponent
             significand_output[overflow] = 0
-            significand_output[input_nan] = 1 << (output_dtype.fp_mantissa_width - 1)
         else:
             exponent_output[overflow] = max_exponent - 1
             significand_output[overflow] = (1 << output_dtype.fp_mantissa_width) - 1
         exponent_output[nonfinite] = max_exponent
-        significand_output[nonfinite & ~input_nan] = 0
+        significand_output[input_inf] = 0
+        # if the input was NaN but conversion erased all its mantissa bits,
+        # set one bit so the output remains NaN.
+        significand_output[input_nan] = 1 << (output_dtype.fp_mantissa_width - 1)
     if output_dtype in (tl.float8e4b8, tl.float8e5b16):
         # FNUZ formats have only unsigned zero; the sign bit alone encodes NaN.
         zero_output = (exponent_output == 0) & (significand_output == 0)

commits.message:
[AMD] Add ScopedNoAliasAA to the MIR scheduling DAG emitter (#12551)

The DAG emitted under TRITON_DUMP_MIR is built with BasicAA alone, while
the MIR-to-ASM pipeline right next to it adds
createScopedNoAliasAAWrapperPass() for a documented reason: without it
BasicAA cannot prove async buffer loads (BUFFER_LOAD_DWORDX4_LDS) do not
alias LDS reads (DS_READ), and the spurious dependencies cost ~30%.

So the DAG we hand to users describes a more constrained problem than
the one the scheduler actually solves. Anything that consumes it to
reason about legal reorderings is told that async-copy-into-LDS cannot
move across an LDS read, when the compiler emitting the code knows it
can.

[NFC] Migrate from deprecated mlir Op::create builder (#12545)

### Description

MLIR has deprecated autogenerated Op::create methods which take a mixed
(containing both Properties and Attributes) attributes list. Instead we
need to use an overload where they are passed separately. This change
updates the uses of this builder and removes the
`-Wno-error=deprecated-declarations` build flag.

https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/219194
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/219195
